messages.author: cab04b8f0759c712
messages.subject: c++: how to test types?
parts:
Is typeid() safe to use for testing types for individual platforms? http://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Typeid

I want to lean on some of our template metaprograms that return types, like return_type. We currently don't have any unit tests for these functions. I want to get some unit tests in there to verify that return_type does the right thing for a combination of template arguments like double, var, fvar<double>, fvar<var>, fvar<fvar<double>>, ...

I know that typeid() is platform dependent, but is it going to work cross platform if I test strings? (I can't see how that wouldn't work, except if on some system it shows var and fvar as the same thing, like "object".)

Is there a better way to approach it?



Daniel

messages.author: 8aa9b8cc06fdc99c
messages.subject: Re: [stan-dev] c++: how to test types?
parts:
Why not just use another metaprogram?

The Boost type traits package has everything you should need:

http://www.boost.org/doc/libs/1_53_0/libs/type_traits/doc/html/index.html

and in particular, is_same:

http://www.boost.org/doc/libs/1_53_0/libs/type_traits/doc/html/boost_typetraits/reference/is_same.html

- Bob
